320	The Sefer HaTemuna, the "Kadmon," writes that Moshe and Tzipporah were buried in the Cave
321	of Machpelah.
322	Did you hear that? Moshe?
323	He didn't enter the Land, so how is he buried in the Cave of Machpelah?
324	No, this is an enormous question.
325	Now, the Sefer HaTemuna is ancient, and the Rav Chida writes this
326	and doesn't comment on it.
327	So it seems he accepted what it says.
328	But this is against an explicit verse in the Torah, and the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi, also writes that once Yaakov was buried,
329	the cave never again received any person into it.
330	The only thing that was buried there besides Yaakov is the head of Esav, on page 13 in Tractate Sotah,
331	but that was even before Yaakov was buried.
332	First the head of Esav was there, and then Yaakov was buried.
333	So if that's the case...
334	then the Zohar is right: after Yaakov was buried it received nothing, not even a head, because it received the head before.
335	So what is the Sefer HaTemuna saying, that Tzipporah and Moshe are buried in the Cave of Machpelah?
336	And he gave a hint to it: "Me'arat Sedeh HaMachpelah" are the initials of Moshe.
337	"Me'arat Sedeh HaMachpelah," the initials of Moshe.
338	Isn't this very puzzling?
339	So what, just because you got initials?
340	You put Moshe into the cave?
341	That surely cannot be.
342	It is a tradition he received.
343	What?
344	And if you got initials, I don't know, what...
345	Condoleezza Rice.
346	So what, was she there?
347	It cannot be.
348	And it also contradicts the Torah, which says that he did not enter the Land of Israel.
349	What's going on here?
350	Moshe, how do you answer this?
351	Sparks.
352	Sparks.
353	An aspect, an aspect.
354	That's it, an aspect of Yaakov, Moshe Rabbeinu.
355	An aspect.
356	But no, if you were saying something good, I would say it's good.
357	Forget it, forget it.
358	In the Zohar, he did not enter the Land of Israel even in his lifetime.
359	Zohar Chukat 183, page a, there I want to bring an answer.
